intent.raw_query: Portugal Algarve, $2200, beach holiday with wine tasting, September 2026 from London

selected_hotel.name: Praia da Marinha, Lagoa Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Praia da Marinha Coastal Hike & Swim
experiences.description: Explore one of the Algarve's most stunning beaches, known for its dramatic golden limestone cliffs, sea caves, and crystal-clear turquoise waters. Hike the clifftop trail and descend to the secluded cove for a swim among natural rock arches.

experiences.name: Algarve Wine & Vineyard Tour
experiences.description: Visit local Algarve wineries such as Quinta dos Vales or Adega do Cantor near Lagoa, sampling regional varieties including Negra Mole and Arinto. Guided tours typically include cellar visits, vineyard walks, and tastings of 5–6 wines paired with local cheeses and charcuterie.

experiences.name: Benagil Sea Cave Kayak Tour
experiences.description: Paddle by kayak from Praia de Benagil into the famous Algar de Benagil sea cave, one of the world's most beautiful natural grottos. A guided 2-hour kayak tour takes you through hidden caves and arches along the dramatic coastline inaccessible by foot.

experiences.name: Tavira Old Town & Roman Bridge Cultural Walk
experiences.description: Wander through the charming historic town of Tavira, crossing its ancient Roman bridge over the Gilão River, visiting the Moorish castle ruins, and exploring whitewashed churches and traditional azulejo tile facades. Stop at a local tasca for a petiscos (tapas) lunch with regional wines.

experiences.name: Ria Formosa Natural Park Sunset Boat Tour
experiences.description: Cruise through the stunning Ria Formosa lagoon system, a protected natural park of barrier islands, tidal flats, and wildlife. Spot flamingos, herons, and seahorses while sailing past golden sandbar islands at sunset, with a glass of local Algarve sparkling wine on board.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Portugal Algarve
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Praia da Marinha, Lagoa Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Faro Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Collect luggage, arrange ground transport (bus or shared shuttle to Lagoa area, ~€5–8 by regional bus via Eva Transportes).
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to Lagoa Boutique Stay in Praia da Marinha. Freshen up, then take a short walk down to the iconic Praia da Marinha beach (5–10 min walk). Explore the dramatic golden limestone cliffs, sea caves, and crystal-clear coves. Swim or simply relax and soak in the scenery.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll into the village of Carvoeiro (3 km away, reachable by taxi ~€6 or a scenic coastal walk). Explore the charming whitewashed village, watch the sunset from Carvoeiro cliffs, and enjoy the laid-back atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Grab a snack or coffee at the airport upon arrival.
meals.lunch: Pick up a fresh baguette sandwich or pastéis de nata from a local bakery/café near Lagoa town (~€3–5).
meals.dinner: Tasca do Zé in Carvoeiro or a local petiscos bar — try grilled sardines or prego (steak sandwich) with a glass of house wine (~€10–14 per person).

day_by_day.notes: September is ideal — warm sea temperatures (~22°C), fewer crowds than July/August, and lower prices. Buy a rechargeable Vamus Algarve bus card at Faro Airport for budget transport throughout the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning visit to Praia da Marinha at sunrise — the golden light on the cliffs is spectacular and the beach is nearly empty. Bring a snorkel if you have one; the rocky outcrops host rich marine life. Explore the clifftop walking trail (Percurso dos Sete Vales Suspensos trailhead is nearby).
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take a short taxi (~€5) to Praia de Benagil. Book a budget sea cave kayak tour or join a shared boat trip to the famous Benagil Cave (Algar de Benagil) — shared group tours cost ~€10–15 per person. The cave's natural skylight dome is one of the Algarve's most iconic sights.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagoa town for the evening. Visit the local market area and browse the weekly produce stalls if open. Enjoy a relaxed dinner in Lagoa.

meals.breakfast: Café at the accommodation or a local pastelaria — coffee + croissant + orange juice (~€3–4).
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic from the Lagoa supermarket (Pingo Doce or Lidl) — local cheese, presunto, olives, crusty bread, and local wine (~€5–7).
meals.dinner: O Leão in Lagoa town — traditional Algarvian cuisine, grilled fish of the day with vegetables and local wine (~€12–15 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Book the Benagil Cave boat/kayak tour in advance online or at Benagil beach to secure the cheapest shared-group rate. Arrive at Benagil early afternoon to avoid peak morning crowds.

day_by_day.morning: Hike the famous Seven Hanging Valleys Trail (Percurso dos Sete Vales Suspensos) — a stunning 5.7 km clifftop trail starting from Praia de Vale Centeanes near Carvoeiro, ending at Praia da Marinha (or reverse). Free to walk, breathtaking sea views, hidden beaches below.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the hike, cool off at Praia de Albandeira — a quiet, sheltered cove accessible via a short path, perfect for swimming. Far fewer tourists than Marinha. Spend the afternoon relaxing on the sand.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Ferragudo village (10 km east, ~€8 taxi or regional bus). Wander the charming fishing village, visit the 16th-century Castelo de São João do Arade (exterior free), and watch the boats on the Arade River estuary.

meals.breakfast: Full Portuguese breakfast at a local café — coffee, toast with butter and jam, fresh orange juice (~€3–5).
meals.lunch: Bring trail snacks and water for the hike. Stop at a beach kiosk at Praia de Albandeira for a simple sandwich or ice cream (~€4–6).
meals.dinner: Restaurante Sueste in Ferragudo — riverside setting, fresh grilled fish, house wine. Budget-friendly for the quality (~€13–16 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Wear sturdy shoes and bring plenty of water for the clifftop hike. The trail is well-marked with yellow and red waymarks. September sun is still strong — apply sunscreen generously.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Portimão (8 km west, ~€2 by regional bus). Visit the Museu de Portimão — a fascinating free or low-cost museum (€3) built inside a former sardine canning factory, covering Algarve history, archaeology, and the fishing industry.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take a short bus to Praia da Rocha — one of the Algarve's most famous beaches, wide golden sands with dramatic rock formations. Swim, sunbathe, and explore the rock pools at the western end near the Fortaleza de Santa Catarina (free entry, great views over the Arade River mouth).
day_by_day.evening: Explore Portimão's riverside promenade and evening market stalls. The town is famous for grilled sardines — enjoy them fresh at a riverside tasca.

meals.breakfast: Coffee and pastel de nata at a café near the accommodation (~€2–3).
meals.lunch: Grab a bifana (pork sandwich) or fresh sardine roll from a beach kiosk at Praia da Rocha (~€4–6).
meals.dinner: Taberna da Maré or a riverside sardine grill in Portimão — grilled sardines, salad, bread, and a carafe of house wine (~€10–13 per person). September is the tail end of sardine season — don't miss it!

day_by_day.notes: The regional Vamus bus connects Lagoa/Carvoeiro area to Portimão frequently. Check the Vamus Algarve app for timetables. Portimão also has a large Lidl and Pingo Doce for restocking budget supplies.

day_by_day.morning: Wine tasting day! Visit Adega do Cantor (Winery owned by Cliff Richard) near Guia/Albufeira (20 km east, ~€12 taxi or bus + short walk). They offer guided cellar tours and tastings of Algarve wines at reasonable prices (~€10–15 for tour + tasting). Alternatively, visit Quinta dos Vales winery near Estômbar (10 km, more accessible) — tastings from ~€10.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the wine theme at a second winery: Quinta da Penina or Adega José de Sousa (slightly further but worth it). Purchase a bottle of local Algarve red or white wine to enjoy at the accommodation. The Algarve produces excellent Negra Mole and Arinto grape varieties.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Praia da Marinha area. Enjoy your purchased wine on the clifftops at sunset — one of the most romantic and budget-friendly evening experiences in the Algarve.

meals.breakfast: Yoghurt, fruit, and bread from the supermarket at the accommodation (~€2–3).
meals.lunch: Many wineries offer light cheese and charcuterie tasting boards to accompany wines (~€8–12) — this can serve as a light lunch.
meals.dinner: Cook a simple meal at the accommodation using local supermarket ingredients — fresh Algarve tomatoes, local cheese, olives, bread, and a bottle of local wine (~€8–10 total).

day_by_day.notes: Book winery visits in advance by email or phone — September is harvest season (vindima) and wineries may be busier than usual. Quinta dos Vales near Estômbar is the most accessible from Lagoa without a car (short taxi ride ~€8).

day_by_day.morning: Explore Silves — the medieval Moorish capital of the Algarve (15 km north of Lagoa, ~€3 by regional bus). Visit the magnificent red sandstone Castelo de Silves (€2.80 entry, one of the best-preserved Moorish castles in Portugal) with panoramic views over orange groves and the Arade River valley.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Silves town: the Gothic Sé Cathedral (free entry), the Roman bridge, and the charming cobblestone streets. Browse the local market if it's a market day. Visit the Museu Municipal de Arqueologia (€2) for Algarve history.
day_by_day.evening: Stay for dinner in Silves — the town is known for excellent, authentic, and affordable local restaurants away from the tourist coast.

meals.breakfast: Coffee and tosta mista (toasted ham and cheese sandwich) at a local café in Lagoa before catching the bus (~€3–4).
meals.lunch: Café Inglês in Silves (set inside the castle walls) or a local tasca — cataplana de peixe (fish stew) or grilled chicken piri-piri (~€9–13 per person).
meals.dinner: Restaurante Marisqueira Rui in Silves — a local institution, famous for affordable fresh seafood and cataplana. House wine is excellent (~€12–15 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Silves is easily reached by regional bus from Portimão or Lagoa. The town is far less touristy than the coast, prices are noticeably lower, and the atmosphere is authentically Portuguese. September's orange and almond harvests make the surrounding countryside particularly scenic.

day_by_day.morning: Beach day at Praia de Carvalho — a hidden gem near Praia da Marinha, accessible via a short tunnel through the cliff. Arrive early to secure a spot on this tiny, sheltered, turquoise-water cove. Bring snorkelling gear for excellent underwater visibility.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk the coastal path westward from Praia da Marinha toward Praia do Paraíso and Praia de Albandeira. These quieter beaches see far fewer visitors in the afternoon. Explore sea caves accessible at low tide (check tide times in advance).
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner drinks at a clifftop bar in Carvoeiro — Cocktail Bar Calypso or a similar spot with ocean views. Enjoy a local beer (Super Bock or Sagres, ~€2–3) or a glass of vinho verde while watching the sunset.

meals.breakfast: Full homemade breakfast at the accommodation — bread, local honey, fresh fruit, coffee (~€3–4 from supermarket supplies).
meals.lunch: Packed lunch from the supermarket — tuna salad, olives, crusty bread, local cheese, sparkling water (~€5–6). Eat on the beach.
meals.dinner: O Castelo restaurant in Carvoeiro or a local tasca — grilled lulas (squid) or arroz de marisco (seafood rice) with house wine (~€12–15 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Praia de Carvalho's tunnel entrance can be tricky at high tide — check tide tables at visitportugal.com or a local surf shop. This is a rest and recharge day after the inland excursion yesterday.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip west to Lagos (30 km, ~€4 by regional bus from Portimão). Lagos is one of the Algarve's most charming historic towns. Explore the 15th-century old town walls, the Igreja de Santo António (baroque church, ~€3 entry), and the Mercado de Escravos (slave market museum, ~€3).
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to Ponta da Piedade — a spectacular headland of golden rock arches, grottos, and sea stacks just south of Lagos. Free to visit, with a short walk from town (~2 km). Take a short boat trip from Lagos marina into the sea grottos (~€10–15 shared tour). Swim at Praia do Camilo — a stunning small beach below the cliffs.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Lagos town in the evening — the pedestrianised Rua 25 de Abril has bars, restaurants, and a lively but not overly touristy atmosphere. Great people-watching from a café terrace.

meals.breakfast: Café stop in Lagos old town after arriving by bus — coffee and pastel de nata (~€2–3).
meals.lunch: O Camilo restaurant near Praia do Camilo, or a simple beach kiosk — fresh grilled fish sandwich or salad (~€8–12).
meals.dinner: : A Forja restaurant in Lagos — a local favourite, excellent grilled fish and meat at very reasonable prices, always busy with locals (~€11–14 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Lagos is easily one of the highlights of any Algarve trip. The regional bus from Portimão to Lagos runs frequently (every 30–60 min). Allow at least 45 minutes to walk to Ponta da Piedade and back from the town centre.

day_by_day.morning: Second wine tasting excursion — visit the Algarve Wine Route (Rota dos Vinhos do Algarve). Head to Adega Cooperativa de Lagoa — the local cooperative winery right in Lagoa town, one of the oldest and most affordable wine experiences in the Algarve. Tours and tastings from ~€5–8, with the option to buy bottles directly at cooperative prices.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the local Lagoa market (if Wednesday or Saturday) or browse the town's shops and artisan stalls. Pick up local products: fig and almond sweets (Dom Rodrigo), medronho (arbutus berry spirit), local olive oil, and dried figs — all excellent budget souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset walk along the cliffs between Praia da Marinha and Praia de Benagil (eastward). The evening light on the limestone cliffs turns everything amber and gold. Return for a quiet evening at the accommodation.

meals.breakfast: Café in Lagoa town — galão (milky coffee) and tosta mista (~€3–4).
meals.lunch: Snack bar or café in Lagoa — prato do dia (daily special) usually includes soup, main course, bread, and drink (~€7–9 per person — excellent value).
meals.dinner: Cook at the accommodation using local market produce — fresh vegetables, local fish from the market, and a bottle of cooperative wine purchased this morning (~€8–10 total).

day_by_day.notes: The Adega Cooperativa de Lagoa is within walking distance of the accommodation area. Call ahead to confirm tour times. The cooperative produces both table wines and the famous Lagoa DOC wines — excellent quality at very low prices.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip east to Albufeira (20 km, ~€3 by regional bus). Visit the old town — the original fishing village with whitewashed houses, narrow lanes, and the famous Arco (arch). Explore the clifftop viewpoints and the lively local market.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the local bus or walk (20 min) to Praia dos Pescadores (Fishermen's Beach) in central Albufeira — wide, sandy, and still beautiful. Then walk east along the coastal path to the quieter Praia de São Rafael and Praia da Galé — more dramatic rock formations and clearer water, away from the Albufeira crowds.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Albufeira old town for the evening. The area is lively but can be touristy — stick to the local side streets away from the strip for more authentic and affordable options.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the accommodation before departure.
meals.lunch: Snack bar near Praia dos Pescadores — fresh grilled fish, salad, and a beer (~€9–12 per person).
meals.dinner: Tasca do Viegas in Albufeira old town — a local institution serving traditional Algarvian food at very fair prices, popular with Portuguese locals (~€10–14 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Albufeira can be crowded and touristy, especially around the 'Strip' area — avoid that zone for an authentic experience. The old town and the fishing beach area are genuinely charming. September sees significantly fewer British package tourists than peak summer.

day_by_day.morning: Relaxed morning at Praia da Marinha — your home beach. Take a final long swim in the crystal-clear waters, explore any sea caves you haven't visited yet, and enjoy the beach at a leisurely pace. Bring a book and simply unwind.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Slide & Splash water park near Lagoa if travelling with family (€25–30 entry — slightly over budget but worth it as a one-off treat), OR alternatively take a free afternoon to explore the Monchique mountain range by bus from Portimão. Caldas de Monchique is a charming spa village with free thermal spring water fountains (~€3–4 bus each way).
day_by_day.evening: Sunset at Praia de Benagil — watch the last light illuminate the famous cave arch from the beach above. This is a magical, free, and unforgettable experience.

meals.breakfast: Relaxed breakfast at the accommodation — fresh fruit, yoghurt, local honey, coffee (~€3–4).
meals.lunch: Beach kiosk at Praia da Marinha or Benagil — toasted sandwich, salad, and a cold beer (~€7–9).
meals.dinner: Splurge slightly for a special penultimate-full-day dinner — Restaurante Vila Lisa in Mexilhoeira Grande (near Portimão) is a legendary, rustic, family-run restaurant serving incredible traditional Algarvian food at very reasonable prices (~€15–18 per person including wine). Book in advance.

day_by_day.notes: Vila Lisa restaurant requires a reservation and is slightly off the beaten path (taxi ~€12–15 from Lagoa) but is widely considered one of the most authentic and affordable quality dining experiences in the entire Algarve. Worth the splurge on your penultimate full day.

day_by_day.morning: Final beach morning — choose your favourite beach from the trip for one last swim. Praia da Marinha at low tide reveals spectacular rock pools and hidden caves worth one final exploration. Take photos, collect a small pebble or shell as a free souvenir.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Ferragudo for a final afternoon stroll — visit the local fish market (mercado de peixe) if open, buy some local produce, and enjoy the peaceful riverside atmosphere. Cross the river mouth to Portimão by water taxi if available (~€2) for a unique perspective.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in the Carvoeiro or Lagoa area. Visit a local adega (wine shop) and pick up bottles of Algarve wine, medronho spirit, or local almond sweets to take home. Enjoy a farewell dinner.

meals.breakfast: Final full Portuguese breakfast at a local café — coffee, fresh orange juice, tosta mista, pastel de nata (~€5–6).
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a riverside café in Ferragudo — soup and bread, or a simple fish dish (~€7–9).
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at a favourite restaurant from the trip, or try Restaurante Boneca in Carvoeiro — fresh seafood, local wine, relaxed atmosphere (~€13–16 per person). Toast to a wonderful Algarve adventure!

day_by_day.notes: Pack your bags this evening and prepare for departure tomorrow. Keep a small bag accessible for airport day use. Check the Vamus bus schedule to Faro Airport for the next morning — book a taxi in advance if the bus timing doesn't align with your flight.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — enjoy a last coffee and pastel de nata at a local café before checking out. If time allows before departure, take one final clifftop walk above Praia da Marinha to say goodbye to the dramatic Algarve coastline.
day_by_day.afternoon: Transfer to Faro Airport. Regional bus via Portimão (~€4–6) or pre-booked taxi/shuttle (~€25–35 shared). Allow at least 2 hours before your flight for check-in and security. Browse the airport shops for any last-minute Portuguese souvenirs — tinned fish, wine, and pastéis de nata are all available airside.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Faro Airport. Carry wonderful memories of 13 days of stunning beaches, golden cliffs, excellent local wine, fresh seafood, and authentic Portuguese culture — all on a budget!

meals.breakfast: Final coffee and pastry at a local café before checkout (~€3–4).
meals.lunch: Light snack at Faro Airport — airport prices are higher, so bring snacks from the supermarket if possible (~€5–8).
meals.dinner: On the flight or upon arrival at your home destination.

day_by_day.notes: Total estimated budget for 13 days (excluding flights and accommodation): approximately €400–550 per person, covering local transport, meals, activities, wine tastings, and a few small souvenirs. September pricing is 15–25% lower than peak July/August, making it an ideal budget travel month in the Algarve.

trip_options.title: Classic Portugal Algarve Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

hotel.name: Praia da Marinha, Lagoa Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Flight arrives at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Collect luggage, pick up rental car at Faro Airport, and drive ~45 minutes west to Praia da Marinha, Lagoa. Check in to the Boutique Stay and freshen up.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a gentle first look at Praia da Marinha beach, just steps from the hotel. Walk the cliffside path for stunning views of the golden limestone arches and sea caves. Settle in, unpack, and orient yourself with the local area.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll into the nearby village of Carvoeiro for a relaxed welcome dinner. Explore the small promenade and watch the sunset over the Atlantic from the clifftop viewpoints.

meals.breakfast: Grab something light at the airport or a café near Faro on arrival
meals.lunch: Quick bite at a roadside café or petrol station snack during the drive to Lagoa
meals.dinner: Restaurante O Castelo in Carvoeiro — mid-range Portuguese seafood, grilled fish and local wine, approx €25–35 per person

day_by_day.notes: Pick up a rental car at Faro Airport — essential for exploring the Algarve. September weather is warm (24–28°C) with minimal rain, perfect beach conditions. Confirm boutique stay check-in time in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning swim and exploration at Praia da Marinha. Arrive before 9:00 AM to enjoy the beach before day-trippers arrive. Walk the coastal trail east toward Benagil for dramatic cliff scenery.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a guided kayak or small boat tour from Benagil Beach to visit the famous Benagil Sea Cave (Algar de Benagil). Book in advance — tours depart regularly and last 1–2 hours. Return to the hotel for a midday rest.
day_by_day.evening: Drive 10 minutes to the town of Lagoa for a local evening. Visit the Adega Cooperativa de Lagoa, one of the oldest wine cooperatives in the Algarve, for a late-afternoon tasting of local Algarve wines including Negra Mole and Crato Branco.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the boutique stay or a local pastelaria — pastel de nata, fresh OJ, coffee
meals.lunch: Beachside snack bar near Benagil — grilled sardine sandwich or prego roll, approx €8–12
meals.dinner: Restaurante Quatro Águas in Lagoa town — traditional Algarvian cuisine, cataplana de peixe, approx €20–30 per person

day_by_day.notes: Book Benagil cave boat tour at least 1 day in advance — very popular in September. Wear water shoes and bring sunscreen. Adega de Lagoa wine tasting is affordable (€5–10) and highly recommended for wine enthusiasts.

day_by_day.morning: Drive 20 minutes west to Portimão and visit the Museu de Portimão, a fascinating free or low-cost museum built inside a former sardine canning factory. Learn about the region's fishing and industrial heritage.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Praia da Rocha, Portimão's iconic beach with wide golden sands and dramatic red rock formations. Spend the afternoon swimming, sunbathing, and walking the beach promenade. Rent a sunbed for comfort (€8–12).
day_by_day.evening: Stay in Portimão for dinner. The Portimão waterfront (Ribeirinha) is famous for grilled sardines — a true Algarve tradition. Join locals at one of the open-air riverside restaurants.

meals.breakfast: At the boutique stay or local café in Carvoeiro
meals.lunch: Casual beach bar at Praia da Rocha — mixed salad, grilled fish, local beer, approx €12–18
meals.dinner: Taberna da Maré on the Portimão riverside — renowned for charcoal-grilled sardines and sea bream, approx €18–28 per person

day_by_day.notes: Museu de Portimão is closed on Mondays. Praia da Rocha can be busy in September — arrive by 11 AM for a good spot. Portimão is also a great place to stock up on local wine, olive oil, and fig sweets at the market.

day_by_day.morning: Drive 35 minutes west to Sagres and visit Cabo de São Vicente — the southwesternmost point of continental Europe. Walk the dramatic clifftops, visit the lighthouse, and feel the raw Atlantic wind. A truly awe-inspiring experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Fortaleza de Sagres (Sagres Fortress), a historic promontory fort with panoramic ocean views. Walk the perimeter walls and learn about Portugal's Age of Discovery. Then relax on Praia do Martinhal, a sheltered and beautiful beach near Sagres.
day_by_day.evening: Have dinner in Sagres village — a small, laid-back surfer town with excellent fresh fish restaurants. Return to Praia da Marinha (~1 hour drive) after dinner.

meals.breakfast: Pack a picnic breakfast from the boutique stay or stop at a café in Portimão en route
meals.lunch: Snack bar near Cabo de São Vicente or bring a packed lunch — limited options at the cape itself
meals.dinner: Restaurante Bossa Nova in Sagres — local favourite, fresh tuna steak and grilled octopus, approx €20–30 per person

day_by_day.notes: Bring a light jacket — Cabo de São Vicente is notoriously windy even in September. Sagres is about 1 hour from the hotel; plan for a full day trip. Fuel up the car before heading out — petrol stations are sparse near the cape.

day_by_day.morning: Relaxed morning at Praia da Marinha. Swim, snorkel, or simply enjoy the stunning cove. September water temperatures are around 21–23°C — ideal for swimming. Bring snorkelling gear to explore the rocky outcrops.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive 15 minutes to Silves, the medieval Moorish capital of the Algarve. Visit the impressive red sandstone Castelo de Silves (€3 entry), walk the ancient walls, and explore the old town's narrow streets and cathedral.
day_by_day.evening: Stay in Silves for the evening. Browse the Saturday market stalls if still open, then enjoy dinner in this charming historic town before returning to the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Boutique stay breakfast or pastelaria in Lagoa
meals.lunch: Café Inglês in Silves — a beloved local institution set inside the old town walls, soups, sandwiches and local dishes, approx €10–15
meals.dinner: Restaurante Marisqueira Rui in Silves — famous for shellfish, percebes (barnacles) and grilled lobster, mid-range splurge approx €30–40 per person

day_by_day.notes: Silves is at its best in September before the tourist season fully winds down. The castle is well worth the entry fee. Consider buying local Silves oranges and figs from roadside stalls on the drive back.

day_by_day.morning: Drive 40 minutes east to Albufeira Old Town. Explore the whitewashed streets, cliff-top viewpoints, and the lively Praça Miguel Bombarda. Visit the Igreja de Sant'Ana church and the clifftop miradouro.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the elevator or steps down to Praia dos Pescadores (Fishermen's Beach) in Albufeira — a picturesque beach framed by colourful fishing boats. Swim and relax before exploring the beach strip.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy the Sunday evening atmosphere in Albufeira's Old Town — quieter and more authentic than weekday nights. Browse local craft shops and ceramics before dinner.

meals.breakfast: Boutique stay or café stop en route to Albufeira
meals.lunch: Tasca do Viegas in Albufeira Old Town — traditional petiscos (tapas-style small plates), local wine, approx €12–18
meals.dinner: Restaurante A Ruína in Albufeira — atmospheric cliffside restaurant, fresh seafood with ocean views, approx €25–35 per person

day_by_day.notes: Albufeira can be touristy but the Old Town retains genuine charm, especially on Sunday evenings. Parking is available at the main car park near the Old Town (€1–2/hour). September is a great time to visit — crowds thinner than July/August.

day_by_day.morning: Wine tasting day! Drive 25 minutes north to the Algarve wine region around Lagoa and São Bartolomeu de Messines. Visit Quinta dos Vales winery — one of the top wine estates in the Algarve, offering guided vineyard tours and tastings of their award-winning red and white wines. Book ahead (approx €15–25 per person).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to a second winery — Quinta da Penina or Adega do Cantor (associated with Sir Cliff Richard) near Albufeira for a contrast in style. Enjoy a leisurely tasting paired with local charcuterie and cheese.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel for a restful evening. Pick up a bottle of your favourite wine from the day's tastings and enjoy a sunset glass on your terrace or the hotel's outdoor space.

meals.breakfast: Boutique stay breakfast — fuel up before the wine day
meals.lunch: Light lunch at Quinta dos Vales — many wineries offer a cheese and charcuterie pairing board with tastings, approx €10–15
meals.dinner: Simple and local — Tasca do Lagoa in Lagoa town, traditional bacalhau (salt cod) dishes and local house wine, approx €15–22 per person

day_by_day.notes: Call ahead to book both winery visits — September is harvest season (vindima) and wineries may be busy with grape picking. This is actually the best time of year to visit — you may get to see the harvest in action. Designate a driver or arrange a taxi/tour.

day_by_day.morning: Beach day at Praia de Armação de Pêra — a long, wide sandy beach 15 minutes from the hotel. Less dramatic than Marinha but perfect for a long relaxed swim and sunbathe. Rent a sunbed and parasol.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or drive to the small whitewashed chapel of Nossa Senhora dos Navegantes perched on the beach at Armação de Pêra — a beautiful and photogenic spot. Then visit the local fish market (if open) to see the day's catch.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Praia da Marinha area. Enjoy a sunset walk along the Percurso dos Sete Vales Suspensos (Seven Hanging Valleys Trail) — a 5.7km coastal trail starting near Marinha that offers the most spectacular cliff scenery in the Algarve.

meals.breakfast: Boutique stay or local café
meals.lunch: Beach snack bar at Armação de Pêra — grilled chicken piri-piri, salad and local beer, approx €12–16
meals.dinner: Restaurant near the hotel — O Cantinho da Marinha in Lagoa, fresh fish and regional cataplana stew, approx €20–28 per person

day_by_day.notes: The Seven Hanging Valleys trail is best walked in the late afternoon for golden-hour light. Wear sturdy shoes — the path is rocky in places. Bring water and a camera. Trail is free and accessible from Praia da Marinha car park.

day_by_day.morning: Drive 1 hour east to Tavira — widely considered the most beautiful town in the Algarve. Explore the Roman bridge, the hilltop castle ruins (Castelo de Tavira), and the Igreja de Santa Maria do Castelo. Wander the charming cobbled streets.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the ferry (€1.50 each way) from Tavira to Ilha de Tavira — a barrier island beach within the Ria Formosa Natural Park. Enjoy pristine, uncrowded Atlantic beaches backed by sand dunes. September is perfect — quieter but still warm.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Tavira town for dinner. Tavira has an excellent restaurant scene with a more authentic, less touristy feel than western Algarve towns.

meals.breakfast: Stop at a café in Tavira on arrival — try a bifana (pork sandwich) or tosta mista with coffee
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic for Ilha de Tavira or use the simple beach bar on the island — fresh sandwiches and cold drinks
meals.dinner: Restaurante Bica in Tavira — beloved local restaurant, cataplana de marisco and Alentejo wines, approx €22–32 per person

day_by_day.notes: Tavira is about 1 hour from the hotel — plan for a full day. The ferry to Ilha de Tavira runs regularly in September. Tavira is in the Eastern Algarve (Sotavento) with calmer, flatter beaches compared to the dramatic western cliffs — a great contrast.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Ria Formosa Natural Park from Olhão, 45 minutes east of the hotel. Join a boat tour through the lagoon system — spot flamingos, herons, and seahorses in one of Europe's most important wetland ecosystems. Tours depart from Olhão ferry terminal.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Olhão's famous covered market halls (Mercado de Olhão) — a stunning 1910s red-brick building with fresh fish, seafood, fruit and vegetables. Browse and sample local produce. Walk the old Moorish-influenced quarter (Barreta).
day_by_day.evening: Return toward Lagoa. Stop in Loulé on the way back — a charming inland town known for its crafts and traditional market. Browse the Moorish-style market building and pick up handmade ceramics or local honey as souvenirs.

meals.breakfast: Early café stop in Olhão before the boat tour
meals.lunch: Olhão market hall — buy fresh oysters, smoked fish, olives and bread for a market picnic, approx €10–15
meals.dinner: Restaurante Avenida in Loulé — traditional Algarvian home cooking, pork with clams (carne de porco à Alentejana), approx €15–22 per person

day_by_day.notes: Book the Ria Formosa boat tour in advance — September is still popular. The Olhão market is closed on Sundays. Loulé's indoor market is open Monday–Saturday. This is a great day for birdwatchers — bring binoculars for the lagoon tour.

day_by_day.morning: Relaxed morning at the hotel — sleep in, enjoy a leisurely breakfast, and take a final swim at Praia da Marinha. This is your last full beach day, so savour the stunning cove.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive 20 minutes to Lagos — one of the most vibrant and beautiful towns in the Algarve. Visit the Ponta da Piedade — extraordinary golden rock formations, sea arches and grottoes accessible by clifftop walk or boat. Arguably the most dramatic coastal scenery in Portugal.
day_by_day.evening: Stay in Lagos for the evening. This lively town has a fantastic restaurant and bar scene — perfect for a celebratory near-end-of-trip dinner. Walk the historic old town walls and the slave market museum (Mercado de Escravos).

meals.breakfast: Boutique stay — relaxed final beach morning breakfast
meals.lunch: Snack bar near Ponta da Piedade or packed lunch from the hotel
meals.dinner: Restaurante Adega da Marina in Lagos — excellent mid-range seafood and regional dishes with a lively atmosphere, approx €22–32 per person

day_by_day.notes: Ponta da Piedade boat tours depart from Lagos marina — a 45-minute tour is highly recommended to see the caves from the water. Book at the marina on the day or in advance. Lagos old town is walkable and very photogenic — allow 2 hours to explore.

day_by_day.morning: Final wine tasting experience — visit Herdade dos Grous or another recommended estate near Albufeira or Silves for a premium tasting session paired with local cheese, presunto (cured ham), and carob products. A fitting farewell to Algarve wine culture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the Lagoa/Carvoeiro area for a final afternoon. Visit the Slide & Splash water park near Lagoa if travelling with family, or take a leisurely drive along the coast road stopping at viewpoints you may have missed. Buy final souvenirs in Carvoeiro village — local pottery, wine, medronho brandy.
day_by_day.evening: Special farewell dinner — treat yourself to a slightly elevated dining experience to celebrate the trip. Return to a favourite restaurant or try somewhere new in Carvoeiro.

meals.breakfast: Boutique stay — enjoy a full breakfast on your last full morning
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the winery or a café in Lagoa
meals.dinner: Restaurante Bon Bon in Carvoeiro (Michelin-starred) — splurge farewell dinner, modern Algarvian tasting menu, approx €80–120 per person — OR Restaurante Sancho in Carvoeiro for a mid-range alternative at €25–35 per person

day_by_day.notes: Bon Bon requires advance booking (often weeks ahead) — book before the trip if interested. September is harvest season — look for local medronho (arbutus berry brandy) at roadside stalls, a unique Algarve spirit. Pack your bags tonight for the morning departure.

day_by_day.morning: Check out of the boutique stay. Take one last walk to the clifftop above Praia da Marinha for a final view of the stunning coastline. Drive to Faro Airport (~45 minutes) allowing plenty of time for car return and check-in.
day_by_day.afternoon: Departure from Faro Airport. If flight is in the late afternoon, explore Faro's charming old town (Cidade Velha) — the walled historic centre with the cathedral, bone chapel (Igreja dos Ossos), and peaceful gardens are all within walking distance of the airport.
day_by_day.evening: Flight home — carry memories of golden cliffs, Atlantic waves, and excellent Algarvian wine.

meals.breakfast: Final breakfast at the boutique stay or a café in Lagoa before checkout
meals.lunch: Café or restaurant in Faro Old Town if time allows — Faro has excellent local restaurants near the marina, approx €12–18
meals.dinner: Airport dining or in-flight

day_by_day.notes: Return rental car with a full tank — petrol stations near Faro Airport are convenient. Allow 2 hours before departure for car return, check-in and security. Faro Old Town is only 10 minutes from the airport — perfect for a final morning if your flight is in the afternoon.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Portugal Algarve Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Praia da Marinha, Lagoa Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Praia da Marinha Coastal Hike & Swim
experiences.description: Explore one of the Algarve's most stunning beaches, known for its dramatic golden limestone cliffs, sea caves, and crystal-clear turquoise waters. Hike the clifftop trail and descend to the secluded cove for a swim among natural rock arches.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival & Transfer — Flight LH lands at Faro Airport at 13:00. No morning activities scheduled. Private luxury transfer arranged from Faro Airport to Praia da Marinha, Lagoa Boutique Stay (approx. 45 minutes).
day_by_day.afternoon: Check-in & Property Orientation — Settle into your boutique accommodation, unpack, and enjoy a welcome amenity. Take a leisurely stroll down to Praia da Marinha beach (5-minute walk) to get your first glimpse of the iconic golden limestone cliffs and turquoise waters. Relax on the beach or explore the cliff-top viewpoints at your own pace.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset Aperitivo & Welcome Dinner — Enjoy a pre-dinner glass of local Vinho Verde or a Sagres craft beer on the terrace of your boutique stay as the sun sets over the Atlantic. Head to a nearby fine-dining restaurant in Carvoeiro or Lagoa for a celebratory welcome dinner featuring fresh Algarve seafood.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable (in-flight or at airport)
meals.lunch: Light snack or meal at Faro Airport or grab a charcuterie board and local cheeses from a gourmet deli en route to the hotel
meals.dinner: O Castelo Restaurant, Carvoeiro — elegant clifftop dining with panoramic ocean views, specializing in fresh grilled fish, cataplana seafood stew, and regional Algarve cuisine; reserve a window table in advance

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private airport transfer in advance. Request early check-in if possible. Keep Day 1 light — jet lag and travel fatigue are common. Confirm dinner reservation before arrival.

day_by_day.morning: Praia da Marinha Coastal Hike & Swim — Begin the day with the signature experience: a guided coastal hike along the Seven Hanging Valleys Trail (Percurso dos Sete Vales Suspensos), starting from Praia da Marinha. Marvel at dramatic golden limestone arches, sea caves, and grottos. Descend to the beach for a refreshing morning swim in the crystal-clear waters. The beach is quieter in the morning, making it ideal for snorkeling among the rock formations.
day_by_day.afternoon: Kayak & Sea Cave Exploration — Book a premium private kayaking or stand-up paddleboard tour departing from Praia da Marinha or nearby Benagil. Paddle through the legendary Benagil Sea Cave (Algar de Benagil), one of the most photographed natural wonders in Portugal. A private guided tour ensures exclusivity and the best lighting inside the cave. Return by early afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Wine & Tapas Evening in Lagoa — Drive or arrange a private transfer to the charming town of Lagoa, the wine capital of the Algarve. Visit a local adega (winery) for an early evening wine tasting of Algarve DOC wines. End the evening with a sophisticated tapas dinner at a boutique wine bar.

meals.breakfast: Full Portuguese breakfast at the boutique stay — freshly baked pastéis de nata, local cheeses, presunto (cured ham), fresh fruit, and artisan coffee
meals.lunch: Picnic-style gourmet lunch on the beach or at the clifftop — arranged by the hotel with local bread, olives, regional cheeses, charcuterie, and chilled rosé wine
meals.dinner: Restaurante Vila Lisa, Mexilhoeira Grande (short drive) — Michelin-recommended, celebrated for traditional Algarvian recipes with a refined modern touch; try the amêijoas na cataplana and local Algarve wines

day_by_day.notes: Book the private kayak tour at least 48 hours in advance. Wear reef-safe sunscreen and water shoes for the coastal hike. The Benagil Cave is best visited before 10:00 AM or after 3:00 PM for optimal light and fewer crowds — adjust kayak tour timing accordingly.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise Yoga & Cliff Meditation — Begin the day with a private sunrise yoga or mindfulness session on the clifftops above Praia da Marinha, arranged through the boutique stay. The dramatic coastal scenery provides an unparalleled backdrop. Follow with a refreshing dip in the ocean.
day_by_day.afternoon: Silves — Medieval Castle & Wine Country Exploration — Private transfer inland to Silves, the ancient Moorish capital of the Algarve. Explore the impressive red sandstone Castelo de Silves and the Gothic Cathedral. Afterward, visit Quinta dos Vales, a prestigious Algarve winery just outside Silves, for a premium wine tasting and vineyard tour including their award-winning reds and whites.
day_by_day.evening: Alfresco Dinner in Silves — Dine in the atmospheric old town of Silves before returning to the boutique stay.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely breakfast at the boutique stay with fresh orange juice squeezed from Algarve oranges, yogurt with local honey, and warm croissants
meals.lunch: Quinta dos Vales Estate Lunch — wine-paired light lunch on the vineyard terrace featuring local charcuterie, cheeses, and seasonal dishes
meals.dinner: Marisqueira Rui, Silves — legendary seafood restaurant renowned for the finest cataplana in the Algarve; book well in advance as it is consistently packed with discerning diners

day_by_day.notes: Quinta dos Vales offers premium private tasting experiences with advance booking. Silves is approximately 30–40 minutes inland by car. Consider hiring a private driver for the day to enjoy wine tastings without concern.

day_by_day.morning: Praia de Benagil & Private Boat Charter — Arrange a private luxury boat charter departing from Portimão or Carvoeiro marina. Cruise along the dramatic coastline between Carvoeiro and Albufeira, stopping at hidden sea caves, secluded beaches accessible only by sea, and pristine snorkeling spots. The boat can anchor at Praia de Benagil for a private beach experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Portimão Waterfront & Leisure — Return to port and explore the vibrant Portimão waterfront. Visit the Museu de Portimão for cultural context on the region's sardine canning heritage. Browse boutique shops along the riverside promenade.
day_by_day.evening: Portimão Fine Dining — Enjoy a sunset cocktail at a rooftop bar overlooking the Arade River estuary before dinner at one of Portimão's top restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Continental breakfast at the boutique stay with freshly baked bread, local jams, smoked salmon, and premium coffee
meals.lunch: Gourmet lunch aboard the private boat charter — pre-arranged with the charter company: fresh seafood platter, chilled white wine, and seasonal fruit
meals.dinner: Taberna da Praça, Portimão — sophisticated Portuguese tavern serving elevated regional classics in a beautifully restored historic building; excellent local wine list

day_by_day.notes: Private boat charters typically cost €400–€900 depending on vessel size and duration. Book at least one week in advance in September. Bring reef-safe sunscreen, a hat, and a light layer for the boat.

day_by_day.morning: Praia da Rocha & Fortaleza de Santa Catarina — Drive 20 minutes to Praia da Rocha, one of the Algarve's most spectacular urban beaches, known for its towering amber rock formations. Explore the 17th-century Fortaleza de Santa Catarina perched above the beach for panoramic views. Enjoy a morning swim at a quieter section of the beach.
day_by_day.afternoon: Algarve Wine Route — Quinta do Barradas & Adega do Cantor — Embark on a curated private wine route through the Algarve interior. Visit Adega do Cantor (the winery associated with Cliff Richard) near Guia for a premium tasting of their celebrated Vida Nova wines. Continue to another local quinta for a comparative tasting of Algarve DOC wines.
day_by_day.evening: Romantic Clifftop Dinner — Return to the Carvoeiro/Marinha area for a memorable clifftop dinner as the sun sets over the Atlantic.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at the boutique stay — eggs Benedict with smoked salmon, fresh pastries, and freshly squeezed juices
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a beachside café at Praia da Rocha — grilled sea bass, house salad, and local white wine
meals.dinner: Bon Bon Restaurant, Carvoeiro — Michelin-starred dining experience offering a creative tasting menu that celebrates Algarve produce with refined contemporary techniques; essential to book weeks in advance

day_by_day.notes: Bon Bon is one of the Algarve's most coveted Michelin-starred restaurants — reservations must be made well in advance. The tasting menu typically runs 6–8 courses with optional wine pairing. Budget approximately €150–€200 per person.

day_by_day.morning: Leisure Morning at Praia da Marinha — A relaxed, unscheduled morning. Sleep in, enjoy a leisurely breakfast, and spend the morning on the beach or by the pool. Read, snorkel, or simply soak in the extraordinary natural beauty of Praia da Marinha. This is one of the least crowded mornings as day-trippers tend to arrive later.
day_by_day.afternoon: Algar Seco Cliff Walk & Carvoeiro Village — Walk the dramatic cliff-top path from Carvoeiro to Algar Seco, a stunning geological formation of sculpted limestone rocks, natural pools, and sea arches. Explore the whitewashed fishing village of Carvoeiro, browse artisan shops, and enjoy a café stop. Visit the Algar Seco Parque viewpoint for spectacular photography.
day_by_day.evening: Private Chef Dinner Experience — Arrange for a private chef to prepare an exclusive in-villa or boutique-stay dinner using the finest local ingredients — fresh-caught fish, Algarve clams, seasonal vegetables, and local wines. This intimate experience elevates the luxury quotient of the trip.

meals.breakfast: Indulgent late breakfast at the boutique stay — avocado toast, smoked salmon, granola with local honey, and a Bloody Mary or fresh juice
meals.lunch: O Castelo Café, Carvoeiro — light lunch of fresh grilled sardines, tomato salad, and local bread on a terrace with sea views
meals.dinner: Private chef in-accommodation dinner — curated 4-course menu with wine pairing; arrange through the boutique stay concierge at least 3 days in advance

day_by_day.notes: Private chef experiences in the Algarve typically cost €120–€250 per person including ingredients and wine. The boutique stay concierge can recommend trusted local chefs. This is an ideal evening for a special occasion or simply a memorable night in.

day_by_day.morning: Sagres & Cabo de São Vicente — Day trip to the southwestern tip of Europe. Private transfer to Sagres (approx. 1 hour). Visit the dramatic Cabo de São Vicente lighthouse, where the Atlantic stretches endlessly to the horizon — one of the most emotionally powerful landscapes in Portugal. Explore the Fortaleza de Sagres, the historic fortress from which Henry the Navigator launched the Age of Discovery.
day_by_day.afternoon: Praia do Beliche & Sagres Exploration — Hike down to the secluded Praia do Beliche, a hidden beach nestled between towering cliffs near Cabo de São Vicente. Swim in the cooler, wilder Atlantic waters. Return to Sagres village to explore the local market and artisan stalls.
day_by_day.evening: Seafood Dinner in Sagres — Dine at one of Sagres' authentic seafood restaurants before the scenic return drive along the Costa Vicentina.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the boutique stay before departure — pastries, cheese, fruit, and strong espresso
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch at Cabo de São Vicente — gourmet hamper prepared by the hotel with local cheeses, charcuterie, olives, crusty bread, and a bottle of chilled Algarve white wine
meals.dinner: Restaurante Mum's, Sagres — beloved local institution known for exceptional fresh fish and seafood at honest prices; try the grilled gilt-head bream or the fish soup

day_by_day.notes: Sagres can be windy even in September — bring a light jacket. The drive along the Costa Vicentina (EN268) back toward Lagos offers spectacular scenery. Consider stopping at Praia da Arrifana on the return for a sunset view.

day_by_day.morning: Lagos Old Town & Ponta da Piedade — Private transfer to Lagos (30 minutes). Explore the beautifully preserved historic center: the 15th-century city walls, the Mercado de Escravos (the world's first slave market museum), and the ornate Igreja de Santo António. Walk to Ponta da Piedade, a breathtaking series of golden rock arches, sea stacks, and emerald grottos — arguably the most photogenic spot in the entire Algarve.
day_by_day.afternoon: Ponta da Piedade Boat Tour & Beach Hopping — Take a private or small-group boat tour from Lagos marina through the Ponta da Piedade grottos, exploring caves and hidden coves inaccessible on foot. Stop at Praia do Camilo and Praia Dona Ana for a swim. These beaches are among the most beautiful in the Algarve.
day_by_day.evening: Lagos Rooftop Cocktails & Dinner — Enjoy sundowner cocktails at a Lagos rooftop bar before a sophisticated dinner in the old town.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at a Lagos café — Pastelaria Mó is celebrated for its artisan pastries and specialty coffee; try the queijada de Lagos (local almond and fig tart)
meals.lunch: Light seafood lunch at a Lagos waterfront restaurant — fresh oysters, grilled squid, and a glass of crisp Algarve white wine
meals.dinner: No Pátio, Lagos — intimate fine-dining restaurant in a romantic courtyard setting; creative modern Portuguese cuisine with exceptional local wine selection

day_by_day.notes: Ponta da Piedade is best photographed in the late afternoon golden hour. The boat tours from Lagos marina last approximately 45–75 minutes. Private tours offer more flexibility and exclusivity.

day_by_day.morning: Spa & Wellness Morning — A dedicated wellness morning at the boutique stay or a nearby luxury spa. Indulge in a signature Portuguese massage using local argan oil and sea salt scrubs, followed by hydrotherapy or a hammam experience. This mid-trip recovery day is essential for sustaining energy through the second week.
day_by_day.afternoon: Algarve Olive Oil & Gastronomy Tour — Join a private guided tour of a local olive grove and artisan olive oil producer in the Algarve hinterland. Learn about traditional pressing methods, taste premium single-estate olive oils, and pair them with local bread, tomatoes, and regional specialties. Visit a local market or farm shop to purchase premium Algarve food products.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset Cruise & Cocktails — Board a premium sunset sailing cruise departing from Carvoeiro or Portimão. Sip Champagne or local sparkling wine as the sun dips below the Atlantic horizon. Return to port for a relaxed late dinner.

meals.breakfast: Spa breakfast at the boutique stay — fresh fruit smoothies, acai bowls, granola, and herbal teas
meals.lunch: Farm-to-table lunch at the olive oil estate — seasonal salads, artisan bread with estate olive oil, local cheeses, and chilled Algarve wine
meals.dinner: Restaurante A Ruína, Albufeira — atmospheric restaurant built into the ruins of a historic building overlooking the old town beach; exceptional seafood and regional Algarve dishes

day_by_day.notes: Book the spa treatment at least 3 days in advance. Sunset cruises in September typically depart around 18:00–18:30. Bring a light cardigan for the boat as evenings can be cooler on the water.

day_by_day.morning: Albufeira Old Town & Falesia Beach — Drive east to Albufeira (35 minutes). Explore the charming Old Town, with its whitewashed buildings, mosaic-tiled streets, and vibrant atmosphere. Walk to the iconic Praia dos Pescadores (Fishermen's Beach) beneath the cliff tunnel. Continue to the spectacular Praia da Falésia — a 6km stretch of dramatic red and ochre cliffs, one of the most visually striking beaches in Portugal.
day_by_day.afternoon: Vilamoura Marina & Golf — Drive to the prestigious Vilamoura Marina (20 minutes from Albufeira). Explore the glamorous marina lined with superyachts, luxury boutiques, and waterfront restaurants. If interested, arrange a round of golf at one of Vilamoura's world-class courses (Victoria, Old Course, or Millennium) — all within minutes of the marina.
day_by_day.evening: Vilamoura Fine Dining — Dine at one of the Algarve's most sophisticated restaurant settings overlooking the illuminated marina.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at a clifftop café in Albufeira old town — fresh pastries, local honey, and strong espresso with sea views
meals.lunch: Praia da Falésia beach club lunch — fresh grilled fish, salads, and chilled rosé at a premium beach club with sun lounger service
meals.dinner: Gusto by Heinz Beck, Conrad Algarve, Vilamoura — Michelin-starred restaurant by celebrated chef Heinz Beck; one of the finest dining experiences in all of Portugal; essential advance reservation

day_by_day.notes: Gusto by Heinz Beck is one of only a handful of Michelin-starred restaurants in the Algarve — this is a highlight dining experience of the trip. Vilamoura golf courses require advance tee-time bookings, especially in September.

day_by_day.morning: Tavira — Eastern Algarve Day Trip — Private transfer to the beautiful town of Tavira in the Eastern Algarve (approximately 1.5 hours). Tavira is widely considered the most elegant and authentically Portuguese town in the Algarve. Explore the Roman bridge, the 37 historic churches, the Moorish castle ruins, and the picturesque Gilão River waterfront.
day_by_day.afternoon: Ilha de Tavira & Ria Formosa Natural Park — Take a short ferry from Tavira to Ilha de Tavira, a pristine barrier island within the Ria Formosa Natural Park. The island's beach stretches for miles with fine white sand and calm, shallow waters — perfect for swimming and relaxation. Explore the natural park's unique lagoon ecosystem.
day_by_day.evening: Tavira Dinner & Return — Dine in Tavira's atmospheric old town before the private transfer back to Praia da Marinha.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the boutique stay before departure — pastries, fresh fruit, and espresso
meals.lunch: Beachside lunch on Ilha de Tavira — fresh grilled fish, prawns, and local salads at a simple but excellent beach restaurant
meals.dinner: Restaurante Aquasul, Tavira — elegant riverside dining with sophisticated Portuguese cuisine, excellent local wines, and romantic atmosphere; try the local Ria Formosa oysters and clams

day_by_day.notes: The drive to Tavira is longer (1.5 hours each way) — a private driver is strongly recommended for comfort. The ferry to Ilha de Tavira runs frequently in September. The Eastern Algarve has a distinctly different, quieter character than the Central Algarve — a rewarding contrast.

day_by_day.morning: Monchique Mountain Escape — Private transfer north into the Serra de Monchique mountains (45 minutes). Visit the charming spa village of Caldas de Monchique, famous for its thermal mineral waters since Roman times. Hike through eucalyptus and cork oak forests to the summit of Fóia (902m), the highest point in the Algarve, for panoramic views stretching to the Atlantic coast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Medronho Tasting & Artisan Shopping — Return to Monchique village to sample medronho, the powerful local arbutus berry spirit, at a traditional distillery. Browse artisan shops for handcrafted wooden goods, local honey, and artisan jams. Visit a local quinta for a tasting of Algarve mountain wines — a very different terroir from the coastal wines.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell Gala Dinner — Return to the Praia da Marinha area for a spectacular farewell dinner at the finest restaurant of the trip — a fitting conclusion to 13 days of luxury in the Algarve.

meals.breakfast: Full Portuguese breakfast at the boutique stay — the works: eggs, local cheeses, presunto, pastries, fresh juice, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch at Restaurante Luar da Fóia, Monchique — traditional mountain cuisine featuring espetada de porco preto (black pork skewers), local sausages, and mountain herbs with stunning valley views
meals.dinner: Bon Bon Restaurant, Carvoeiro (return visit) OR Ocean Restaurant, Vila Vita Parc, Porches — two Michelin-star restaurant by chef Hans Neuner; one of the most acclaimed fine-dining experiences in all of Portugal; exceptional tasting menu with wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Ocean Restaurant at Vila Vita Parc holds two Michelin stars and is consistently ranked among Portugal's best restaurants. Reservations must be made weeks in advance. The tasting menu is approximately €250–€350 per person with wine pairing. This is the crown jewel dining experience of the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Final Morning at Praia da Marinha — A slow, savored final morning. Wake up early for one last sunrise walk along the clifftops above Praia da Marinha. Take a final swim in the crystal-clear waters. Collect any remaining souvenirs — local wines, olive oils, conservas (artisan tinned fish), and ceramics — from nearby shops.
day_by_day.afternoon: Checkout & Departure Transfer — Check out of the boutique stay (typically by 12:00 noon; request late checkout if flight permits). Private luxury transfer to Faro Airport for departure. Reflect on 13 extraordinary days in one of Europe's most beautiful coastal regions.
day_by_day.evening: Departure — Flight home.

meals.breakfast: Final leisurely breakfast at the boutique stay — order everything you loved most over the past 13 days; savor local pastries, cheeses, and the last café com leite
meals.lunch: Light farewell lunch at a nearby café or restaurant in Carvoeiro — fresh seafood sandwich (prego de atum) and a final glass of Algarve white wine
meals.dinner: In-flight or at destination

day_by_day.notes: Request late checkout from the boutique stay to maximize the final morning. Allow at least 2.5 hours before flight departure for the transfer to Faro Airport and check-in. Pack purchased wines and olive oils carefully in checked luggage. Consider purchasing a case of Algarve DOC wine to ship home as a lasting memory of the trip.
